FINDING_ID: ROUND5_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.91  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.86  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.process_round()` can crash on legitimate non-response/exclusion races because it unconditionally updates fingerprints for every `active_model`, but `_live_fingerprints` / `_round_metrics` are only initialised from the original model list.** If `FailureHandler.active_models` is ever polluted with an unknown ID or a model ID accepted through unchecked external input paths, `update_fingerprints()` does `old_fp = self._live_fingerprints[model_id]` and `self._round_metrics[model_id].append(obs)`, both of which are hard KeyErrors. This is distinct from the already-noted trust/integrity issues: the cross-cutting failure is that multiple subsystems assume the active-set is a trusted closed world, but no boundary enforces that invariant. PROPOSED_FIX: make `active_models` derivable only from the manager’s canonical pool, reject unknown model IDs at all public boundaries, and harden `update_fingerprints()` with membership checks against canonical model registry before indexing internal state.

FINDING_ID: ROUND5_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.84  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **Role reassignment can silently orphan the locked PM from the active set while still preserving it in `role_map`, creating a logically impossible configuration that later poisons allocation and abort logic.** `RoleAssignment.reassign()` always emits `{pm_model_id: PM}` even if the PM is no longer in `active_models`. Meanwhile `get_live_models()` filters by `failure_handler.active_models`, so allocation may proceed with no PM in the actual live model pool while `role_map` still claims one exists. This is deeper than the stale-role-map findings: it creates a split-brain system state where Area 1 says PM exists, Area 2 allocates without it, and Area 6 may or may not abort depending on timing. PROPOSED_FIX: enforce invariant `pm_model_id in active_models` before any reassignment; if violated, abort immediately and never publish a new `role_map` containing an inactive PM.

FINDING_ID: ROUND5_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.82  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager` accepts arbitrary caller-owned `tasks` in `process_round()` but never binds them to the allocation that supposedly produced the round, so cost/yield/failure decisions can be computed against a different task universe than the one actually dispatched.** Prior findings noted that `allocation` is dropped and `tasks` unused; the deeper missed issue is semantic desynchronisation across Areas 2, 5, and 6. A caller can dispatch allocation A for tasks set T1, then mistakenly call `process_round(..., tasks=T2, round_cost=c2)`. The manager will still update convergence, stopping, failures, and state transitions as if the round were coherent. This breaks auditability and makes any post-hoc interpretation of `round_cost`, missing responses, and model performance invalid. PROPOSED_FIX: require the exact `Allocation` used for dispatch as an input to `process_round()`, persist it, and validate that all responses/findings are a subset of models/tasks in that allocation before any state mutation.

FINDING_ID: ROUND5_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION: 0.80  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`FailureHandler._expected_performance()` can produce expectations greater than the theoretical maximum actual score, making some models structurally incapable of avoiding underperformance.** Actual performance is `finding_count * mean_abstraction`, unbounded in count but often small in practice; expected performance is a dot product of raw fingerprint components, where `D_decay` is nonnegative and `A/C/v_bar` are treated as if commensurate. Because the baseline vectors are not constrained relative to the actual metric scale, two models with identical operational output can be judged differently purely due to fingerprint magnitude drift. This is not just the already-caught raw-vs-normalised issue; it is a deeper unit mismatch between numerator and denominator. PROPOSED_FIX: redefine expected performance in the same units as actual performance, e.g. expected number of weighted findings per round from empirical history, or normalise actual into the same bounded [0,1] scale before comparison.

FINDING_ID: ROUND5_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.79  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The manager can mutate state after emitting externally visible “stop” and “convergence” events, so observers can act on a transient decision that is invalidated by later side effects in the same call.** `process_round()` emits `CONVERGENCE_CHECK` and `STOP_CHECK` before FSM transition, role reassignment, and fingerprint update. An external callback can observe `converged=False, stop=False` and decide to dispatch another round, but the same call may then trigger `FAIL_CRITICAL` or `MAX` and terminate. This is a cross-cutting event-ordering flaw, not just mislabeled event timing. PROPOSED_FIX: treat events as post-commit notifications: compute all decisions first, transition and mutate state, then emit a final coherent event bundle reflecting the committed round result.

FINDING_ID: ROUND5_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.77  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`ConvergenceDetector` and `DiminishingReturnsDetector` together are not monotone under round overwrite, so replacing a previously stored round can retroactively improve convergence while worsening yield, or vice versa, without any invalidation barrier.** `add_round_findings()` allows overwriting `_round_findings[round_idx]` and selectively clears some caches; `DiminishingReturnsDetector.add_round()` independently overwrites cumulative yield/cost for the same round. Because the manager does not make round indices immutable, repeated processing of the same round can create histories inconsistent across Areas 4 and 5. Some overwrite risk was noted for convergence alone; the missed cross-area issue is that the two detectors can now disagree about what “round r” even means. PROPOSED_FIX: make round submission idempotent-but-immutable: reject duplicate round indices once committed, or clear and recompute all dependent downstream state from a single canonical round ledger.

FINDING_ID: ROUND5_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.75  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.72  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`DynamicManager.__init__()` does not validate that the model pool is non-empty before constructing dependent subsystems, so the public constructor fails indirectly and non-locally.** `RoleAssignment.assign()` eventually raises for empty models, but by that point the top-level API has already partially begun manager construction. This is distinct from prior notes about empty-pool failures in lower layers: the orchestration boundary itself lacks a fail-fast precondition. PROPOSED_FIX: validate `models` at `DynamicManager` entry and raise a direct constructor-level `ValueError("model pool must be non-empty")`.

FINDING_ID: ROUND5_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION: 0.70  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`round_idx` parameters are accepted in multiple APIs but are advisory only, allowing internal histories to become temporally nonsensical without any detection.** `RoleAssignment.reassign(round_idx, ...)` ignores `round_idx`; `FailureHandler.get_recovery(model_id, round_idx, ...)` stores the supplied round but does not verify monotonicity; `ModelResponse.round_idx` and `Finding.round_idx` are consumed by some code and ignored by others. This is broader than the already-caught round-consistency issue: temporal metadata is present throughout the API surface but not treated as an invariant anywhere. PROPOSED_FIX: centralise round authority in `DynamicManager`; reject any caller-supplied object whose embedded `round_idx` differs from the manager’s current round, and remove unused round parameters from internal methods where they are not enforced.

FINDING_ID: ROUND5_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION: 0.66  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`ManagerEventStream` has unbounded memory growth by design, and the manager emits high-volume metadata events containing full live-fingerprint snapshots every round.** `all_events` is permanent, and `update_fingerprints()` appends a `ROUND_COMPLETE` event whose metadata includes every model’s full fingerprint map. In long-running or highly instrumented runs this creates O(rounds × models) retained metadata, independent of whether the caller ever consumes it. This is a cross-cutting observability/resource flaw rather than a simple efficiency nit. PROPOSED_FIX: bound or rotate the permanent event log, make full-state snapshots opt-in, and emit compact delta events by default.

FINDING_ID: ROUND5_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION: 0.64  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`FailureHandler.detect_failure()` conflates transport success with semantic success by evaluating underperformance only after format/parsing checks, but it never emits any event for the underperformance failure it may return.** The FORMAT emission bug was already caught; the missed issue is broader observability inconsistency: one class of failure is visible in monitoring only through later recovery side effects, while other classes are visible at detection time. That makes event consumers unable to distinguish “no failure” from “underperformance detected but silently returned.” PROPOSED_FIX: emit `ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM` immediately when the underperformance predicate triggers, before returning the failure type.

FINDING_ID: ROUND5_F011  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION: 0.61  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **`LoadBalancer._objective()` and `_balanced()` are incompatible with the role-admissibility policy because they score all models, including structurally non-worker PM slots, as if they were part of the balancing target population.** A related penalty issue was found for PM idleness, but the deeper missed point is objective incoherence: the optimization target itself is defined over a resource pool different from the admissible execution pool. That means even a hypothetical optimal solver would be minimizing the wrong function. PROPOSED_FIX: compute balance and bottleneck only over models admissible for the task class under the current allocation regime, or separate worker-balance from reserve/PM-utilization metrics.

FINDING_ID: ROUND5_F012  
SEVERITY: 0.60  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION: 0.58  
VERIFIED: FALSE  
DESCRIPTION: **The self-test smoke path does not exercise the manager’s central orchestration loop at all, so “Phase 6 implementation complete” can print even when the integrated system is unusable.** The module runs reduction validators, prints roles, checks one dispatch-feasibility call, and queries correlated failure probability, but never calls `get_allocation()` followed by `process_round()`. This is deeper than weak validators: the published smoke test omits the only path that actually composes Areas 1–6. PROPOSED_FIX: replace the smoke test with a minimal end-to-end scenario that allocates tasks, processes a round, verifies state advance, verifies event emission order, and checks that live fingerprints and active models evolve coherently.

Definitive stance: there are still missed findings. The most important new issues are cross-area invariant breaks: split-brain PM state, unbound round/task identity, post-event mutation, and the unit mismatch in underperformance scoring.
